title: The People Around Him
subtitle: Family, Friends and Rivals
intro: He was never a solitary figure. A wife who edited him, a sister who raised his daughter, a forester who redrew the map with him, a naturalist who argued with him in Yosemite, and rivals who sharpened him. Fifteen questions on the company Roosevelt kept.
heroAlt: Théobald Chartran's painted portrait of Edith Kermit Roosevelt in a plumed hat, seated on a stone bench in a garden
heroCredit: Théobald Chartran's 1902 portrait of Edith Kermit Roosevelt, photographed by Frances Benjamin Johnston. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

badge.title: The People Around Him
badge.shareText: I scored {score}/{total} on the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library's People quiz — {tier}. Try it:

tiers.name: Tennis Cabinet
tiers.line: You were in the inner circle.

questions.prompt: Which sister did Roosevelt rely on most throughout his life?
questions.explanation: Bamie — the eldest, unmarried for most of her life, and the steadiest person in the family. She raised his daughter Alice after 1884, ran a household that doubled as a political salon, and gave him advice he actually took.
questions.credit: Alice, Corinne, and Anna. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: How long had Roosevelt known Edith Carow before they married?
options: They met during his Badlands years
Since childhood — she was a friend of his sister
questions.explanation: Since they were small children. Edith was Corinne's friend and had been in and out of the Roosevelt house on East 20th Street for years. They married in London in December 1886, after a secretly conducted courtship.
questions.imageAlt: Théobald Chartran's painted portrait of Edith Kermit Roosevelt in a plumed hat, seated on a stone bench in a garden
questions.credit: Théobald Chartran's 1902 portrait of Edith Kermit Roosevelt, photographed by Frances Benjamin Johnston. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: Who was Roosevelt's closest political friend and correspondent for over thirty years?
questions.explanation: Henry Cabot Lodge, senator from Massachusetts. Their correspondence runs to hundreds of letters and is one of the best sources on Roosevelt's private thinking — he wrote to Lodge the things he would not say in public.
questions.credit: Theodore Roosevelt, three-quarter length portrait, seated. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: Which reformer and photographer showed Roosevelt New York's tenements?
questions.explanation: Jacob Riis, author of How the Other Half Lives. Roosevelt read the book, walked into Riis's office and offered to help. Riis went with him on the midnight walks that made his name as police commissioner, and they stayed friends for life.
questions.imageAlt: Roosevelt in his Mulberry Street office as police commissioner
questions.credit: Theodore Roosevelt in his Mulberry Street office when he was police commissioner. The New York Public Library.

questions.prompt: With whom did Roosevelt camp in Yosemite in 1903?
questions.explanation: John Muir, for three nights, having deliberately ditched the official party. They woke one morning under fresh snow. Muir used the time to press the case for federal control of the valley, and got it.
questions.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt and John Muir on Glacier Point
questions.credit: Theodore Roosevelt and John Muir on Glacier Point, Yosemite Valley, California. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: Who was Roosevelt's chief forester and the architect of his conservation policy?
questions.explanation: Gifford Pinchot, first chief of the United States Forest Service. He and Roosevelt worked so closely that when Congress moved to strip the president's power to create forest reserves, Pinchot stayed up over the maps so Roosevelt could proclaim sixteen million acres before signing.
questions.imageAlt: President Roosevelt and Chief Forester Gifford Pinchot
questions.credit: President Theodore Roosevelt and Chief Forester Gifford Pinchot. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: Which Black leader did Roosevelt invite to dine at the White House in 1901?
questions.explanation: Booker T. Washington, founder of Tuskegee Institute — the first time a president had entertained a Black American as a dinner guest at the White House. The reaction across the South was violent enough that Roosevelt never repeated the invitation.
questions.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt and Booker T. Washington at Tuskegee Institute
questions.credit: Theodore Roosevelt and Booker T. Washington at Tuskegee Normal and Industrial Institute. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: Who commanded the Rough Riders above Roosevelt?
questions.explanation: Colonel Leonard Wood, an army surgeon with a Medal of Honor and real campaign experience. Roosevelt turned down the command himself on the grounds that he did not yet know enough, and served as lieutenant colonel under Wood until Wood was promoted.
questions.imageAlt: Roosevelt greeting Colonel Brodie of the Rough Riders
questions.credit: Greeting Col. Brodie of Rough Riders. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: Which New York party boss reluctantly made Roosevelt governor and then tried to get rid of him?
questions.explanation: Senator Thomas Platt, who wanted a war hero on the ticket and assumed he could manage him. Two years later he was working to push Roosevelt into the vice presidency — an office then regarded as a political graveyard.
questions.imageAlt: Campaign poster for Colonel Theodore Roosevelt for Governor
questions.credit: For Governor, Col. Theodore Roosevelt; For Lieut. Governor, Timothy L. Woodruff. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: Which Republican power broker asked whether his party realised there would be only one life between "that madman" and the presidency?
questions.explanation: Mark Hanna of Ohio, McKinley's closest political ally, who opposed putting Roosevelt on the 1900 ticket. Within eighteen months he was proved right in the worst possible way.
questions.imageAlt: Vice President Roosevelt at McKinley's swearing in
questions.credit: Vice-President Roosevelt at the swearing in of President McKinley, March 1901. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: Which friend and cabinet member did Roosevelt promote to the presidency in 1908 and then run against in 1912?
questions.explanation: William Howard Taft, his Secretary of War. Roosevelt chose him, pushed him to the nomination, and then broke with him so completely that he split the Republican Party to oppose him. They reconciled, briefly, near the end of Roosevelt's life.
questions.imageAlt: Cartoon of the 1912 race to the White House
questions.credit: Race to the White House, with Wilson on a donkey and Taft on an elephant. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.

questions.prompt: Which men did Roosevelt bring from Maine to run his Elkhorn Ranch?
questions.explanation: Bill Sewall, a Maine guide he had first hired as a teenager in 1878, and Sewall's nephew Wilmot Dow. Neither had worked cattle. Roosevelt wanted men he trusted, and Sewall was blunt enough to tell him things nobody else would.
questions.imageAlt: Wilmot Dow, Theodore Roosevelt and Bill Sewall at the Elkhorn Ranch
questions.credit: Wilmot Dow, T.R., and Bill Sewall at Elkhorn Ranch. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University. Cropped from the album mount.

questions.prompt: Who guided Roosevelt on his first Dakota buffalo hunt and became his lieutenant in the Badlands?
questions.explanation: Joe Ferris, barn superintendent at the Pyramid Park Hotel, who took the job for a hundred dollars expecting the Easterner to quit. He later ran a store in Medora where Roosevelt wrote part of a book upstairs.
questions.imageAlt: The store of Joe Ferris at Medora, North Dakota
questions.credit: The store of Joe Ferris at Medora, N.D. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: Which French aristocrat founded Medora and became Roosevelt's neighbour and rival in Dakota?
questions.explanation: Antoine de Vallombrosa, the Marquis de Mores, born the same year as Roosevelt. He founded Medora in 1883, named it for his wife, and sank a fortune into a scheme to ship dressed beef east in refrigerated cars. The relationship between the two men was tense and nearly ended in a duel.
questions.imageAlt: The house of the Marquis de Mores above the Little Missouri
questions.credit: The house of the Marquis de Mores from the eastern bank of the river. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.

questions.prompt: Which niece of Roosevelt's became one of the most influential Americans of the twentieth century?
questions.explanation: Eleanor, daughter of his brother Elliott. Roosevelt gave her away at her 1905 wedding to Franklin — and, according to the newspapers, rather stole the occasion. Alice was his daughter, not his niece.
questions.imageAlt: Theodore and Edith Roosevelt seated with five children in a studio group portrait, the youngest a baby
questions.credit: Theodore and Edith Roosevelt with Alice, Ted, Kermit, Ethel and the infant Archie, photographed by C. M. Gilbert, January 1895 — five children; Quentin, the sixth, was born two years later. Theodore Roosevelt Collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University.
